title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student finished laser-cutter training on Monday and chatted with your assistant. The next Monday she opens a new chat. The assistant uses only a model and a calendar tool, with nothing saved. What does it know about her training?

options.text: It knows it, because the model keeps every earlier chat
It knows it, because the calendar tool stores her record
It knows nothing, because the earlier chat's context is gone
It knows it, because its context window is large enough

items.stem: In one request, the system prompt, tool descriptions and question total 1,500 tokens. The model makes four calls, and each of the first three calls ends with a tool request whose result adds 500 tokens to the history. Ignoring the model's own short tool requests, how many input tokens are read across all four calls?
Your sponsor's model has a window big enough to hold all the makerspace manuals. Which is the strongest reason to still search the manuals and send only a few excerpts?

options.text: Manuals pasted into a prompt are rejected by the model
Retrieval is needed because models cannot read long text
Excerpts keep every call cheaper and recall of facts better
A big window makes the model forget the system prompt

items.stem: In one or two sentences: when an agent saves a note about a student for next week, which part of the system actually writes the note to storage, and how does the note get back into the model's view next week?

A student asks about the water-jet cutter's pressure limit. The assistant calls search_manuals, and the search returns the three closest chunks of the water-jet manual. What does the model see when it writes its answer?

options.text: The three chunks, plus the rules, tools and chat so far
The whole water-jet manual, which the search has opened
Only the three chunks, with the chat and rules removed
The index of every manual, ranked by closeness to the question
